benchmark_name: Improving Mental Health Screening and Early Risk Detection in Spanish
authors: Andreu Casamayor-Segarra; Vicent Ahuir; Antonio Molina-Marco; Lluís-F. Hurtado
institutions: VRAIN: Valencian Research Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Universitat Politècnica de València; ValgrAI: Valencian Graduate School and Research Network of Artificial Intelligence
ground_truth_source: MentalRisk shared task datasets (IberLEF 2023 and 2024): user-level labels from Telegram posts for depression, anxiety, and eating disorders (anorexia/bulimia)
size_of_benchmark: MR24-DD: 885 users (train+val+test); MR23-ED: 335 users; MR23-D: 335 users
what_assessed_skills: Domain-adapted language model representations for Spanish mental health discourse; early risk detection timing (when to issue a prediction); classification accuracy under incremental context; latency-accuracy tradeoff
tasks_assessed: Multi-class disorder detection (depression/anxiety/none); Binary eating disorder detection (anorexia/bulimia); Binary depression detection; Early risk detection with incremental context expansion (ICE)
population_represented: Spanish-speaking social media users on Telegram with depression, anxiety, eating disorders, or no disorder
evaluation_method: Automated evaluation using MentalRisk shared task protocol: sequential/incremental prediction rounds; metrics: Macro F1-score, ERDE5, ERDE30, LTP (Latency True Positive). Standard classification also evaluated with Precision, Recall, F1. No human evaluation.
llms_evaluated: RoBERTa-es-mental-large (RoBERTa-large-bne + DAP, 355M params); Longformer-es-mental-base (Longformer-base-4096-bne + DAP, 149M params); Longformer-es-mental-large (RoBERTa-es-mental-large adapted to Longformer, 435M params)
performance_scores: Standard classification best (Longformer-es-m-large): MR24-DD F1=0.907, MR23-ED F1=0.920, MR23-D F1=0.767. Early detection best ICE+100w: MR24-DD F1=0.905 (ERDE30=0.040), MR23-ED F1=0.923 (ERDE30=0.043), MR23-D F1=0.753 (ERDE30=0.139)
short_summary: This paper addresses two challenges in Spanish mental health NLP: lack of domain-adapted Spanish language models and the difficulty of early detection from evolving social media post histories. The authors introduce three Spanish foundational models (RoBERTa-es-mental-large, Longformer-es-mental-base, Longformer-es-mental-large) via domain-adaptive pre-training on ~1.9M translated Reddit mental health posts. They also propose the Incremental Context Expansion (ICE) methodology, which automatically relabels user-level datasets into context-level datasets to train models for early detection. Models are evaluated on three MentalRisk shared task benchmarks (depression, anxiety, eating disorders) using F1, ERDE5, ERDE30, and LTP metrics via fully automated sequential evaluation. Results show that domain-adapted models consistently outperform general-purpose baselines, and ICE further improves early detection by teaching models to delay predictions until sufficient evidence accumulates, achieving new state-of-the-art on most Spanish early-detection tasks.

benchmark_name: The MADRS Pipeline: Supporting Depression Assessment in Clinical Trials
authors: Mila Fodor; Katalin Ócsai; Francesco Periti; Rien Sonck; Alex Boudreau
institutions: Clario, part of Thermo Fisher Scientific
ground_truth_source: Expert MADRS ratings assigned by a reviewer team (senior clinicians) who independently evaluated audio recordings of clinical interviews conducted by trained raters at private clinics; quality labels (Compliant/Non-compliant) derived from discrepancies between rater and reviewer scores
size_of_benchmark: 1,602 interviews (~40 min each); ~16,000 expert-rated MADRS instances; MADRS assessment: 1,100 train / 251 dev / 251 test interviews; Quality assessment: 610 interviews (305 train / 305 test); Transcript segmentation: 14 interviews (3,970 utterances); Transcription: 8 interviews (2,642 utterances)
what_assessed_skills: Automatic depression severity estimation via MADRS scale from clinical interview transcripts; transcript segmentation by symptom item; speech-to-text transcription quality; clinical rating quality/compliance detection
tasks_assessed: Interview transcription (ASR + speaker diarization); Transcript segmentation into 10 MADRS/SIGMA symptom sections (multi-class classification); MADRS symptom severity estimation per item (ordinal regression, 0–6 scale); Quality assessment of clinical ratings (binary classification: Compliant vs. Non-compliant)
population_represented: Patients enrolled in depression clinical trials; interviews conducted by trained clinicians in private clinics following SIGMA guidelines
evaluation_method: Automated evaluation against expert reviewer MADRS scores and quality labels. Metrics: Spearman correlation, MAE, Accuracy@1 (MADRS assessment); weighted F1 / one-vs-all F1 (transcript segmentation); temporal Dice, Jaccard index, cosine embedding similarity (transcription); MCC, TP, TN, FP, FN (quality assessment). Human expert ratings used as ground truth but evaluation process itself is Automated.
llms_evaluated: GPT-4.1 (closed-source; used for transcript segmentation and LLAMADRS baseline); Claude Sonnet 4.5 (closed-source; transcript segmentation and LLAMADRS baseline); Llama 3.3 70B (open-weight; transcript segmentation and LLAMADRS baseline). Encoder models fine-tuned (RoBERTa, ModernBERT, MentalBERT, ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT) are not counted as LLMs for this field.
mental_health_conditions: Depression (assessed via Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale, MADRS)
performance_scores: MADRS Assessment (best model RoBERTa): Spearman=0.867, MAE=2.956, Accuracy@1=0.895. Transcript Segmentation: GPT-4.1 weighted F1=0.983, Claude Sonnet 4.5=0.978, Llama 3.3 70B=0.615. Quality Assessment (Random Forest w/ reviewer scores): MCC=0.704. LLAMADRS baselines: GPT-4.1 Spearman=0.849, Claude Sonnet 4.5=0.848, Llama 3.3 70B=0.851.
short_summary: This paper introduces the MADRS Pipeline, an end-to-end LLM-based system designed to support depression assessment in clinical trials using structured SIGMA interviews. The pipeline processes audio recordings through four sequential components: interview transcription, transcript segmentation into 10 MADRS symptom sections, symptom severity estimation (0–6), and quality assessment of clinical ratings. Evaluated on ~1,602 real clinical trial interviews with expert MADRS ratings, the pipeline compares fine-tuned encoder models (RoBERTa, MentalBERT, etc.) against decoder LLMs (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Llama 3.3 70B) using the LLAMADRS zero-shot prompting baseline. The best-performing model (fine-tuned RoBERTa) achieves a Spearman correlation of 0.867 with expert reviewer ratings on total MADRS scores, outperforming all LLM baselines on MAE and Accuracy@1.

benchmark_name: Cognivia: A Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Copilot for Evidence-Based Mental Healthcare
authors: Qi Chen; Siria Xiyueyao Luo; Jian Wang; Yuan Shi; Haocong Rao; Xuejiao Zhao
institutions: Sichuan University; Southwest Petroleum University; University of Groningen; West China Hospital, Sichuan University; Nanyang Technological University
ground_truth_source: Expert seed set manually curated from core CBT literature (Feeling Good Handbook; Feeling Good: The New Mood Therapy); 100-case subset annotated by professional psychotherapists according to CBT-based guidelines for distortion identification evaluation; 10 behavioral science experts rating 10 test-set samples for human evaluation
size_of_benchmark: Augmented CBT Cognitive Triplet Dataset: 9,437 entries (question, cognitive distortion, rational response triplets); Expert seed set: 296 curated examples; Test set: 1,435 instances (CBT pathway analysis); Human evaluation: 10 samples rated by 10 experts
what_assessed_skills: Cognitive distortion identification; CBT-aligned rational response generation; Therapeutic fidelity; Semantic fidelity; Safety and robustness; Empathy and deployment feasibility; Relational boundary integrity
tasks_assessed: Cognitive distortion identification (classification of 11 distortion types); Rational response generation (structured 5-component CBT responses); CBT-structured dialogue quality assessment
population_represented: General mental health help-seekers; users presenting cognitive distortions; sourced from PsyQA (Chinese online mental health forum posts)
languages: English (model output); Chinese (PsyQA source data, translated to English)
evaluation_method: Both — (1) Automated: BLEU, ROUGE-1/2/L, GLEU (lexical similarity); LLM-as-a-judge with existing criteria (Relevance, CBT Structure, Helpfulness out of 10) and proposed CogEval criteria (12 sub-dimensions on 1–5 Likert scale); (2) Human: 10 behavioral science experts rated 10 test samples using structured CogEval questionnaire with 5-point Likert scale; ICC ≈ 0.95
llms_evaluated: Cognivia (fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (baseline); CBT-LLM; llama-3.2-psychotherapy-cbt-i1-Q6_K; Gemini 3 Flash Preview; PsyCoPref-Llama3-8B-main; Qwen3-235B-A22B; Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct; Mistral Medium 3; GPT-5 Mini
mental_health_conditions: Cognitive distortions (All-or-Nothing Thinking, Overgeneralization, Mental Filter, Discounting the Positive, Mind Reading, Fortune Telling, Magnification or Minimization, Emotional Reasoning, Should Statements, Labeling, Personalization and Blame); general mental health support
performance_scores: Cognivia (best): ROUGE-1=0.592, ROUGE-2=0.166, ROUGE-L=0.246, BLEU-1=0.103, BLEU-2=0.103, GLEU=0.242; Relevance=9.869/10, CBT Structure=9.868/10, Helpfulness=9.868/10; CogEval: SC=4.75, DO=4.93, SS=4.75, CA=4.98, EV=4.90, IC=4.81, CC=4.63, WF=4.91, BF=5.00, NE=5.00, DA=4.99, AR=4.97 (all out of 5)
short_summary: Cognivia is an evidence-based AI therapist that operationalizes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) by automatically identifying cognitive distortions and generating structured rational responses. The system is built on a novel Augmented CBT Cognitive Triplet Dataset (9,437 entries) derived from expert-curated CBT literature seeds and PsyQA mental health Q&A data, using multi-stage prompting with DeepSeek and GPT-5 Mini, then fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct via LoRA. The paper also introduces CogEval, the first hierarchically structured evaluation framework with 12 sub-dimensions across 4 categories for assessing CBT rational responses. Evaluation used BLEU/ROUGE lexical metrics, LLM-as-a-judge scoring with both existing and CogEval criteria, and human assessment by 10 behavioral science experts. Cognivia consistently outperforms 9 strong baselines, achieving top scores across all automatic and human evaluation protocols.
